title: Stopping signs 1: م (must stop) and لا (do not stop): rule card and examples
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Summer 1: At-Tariq 9 to 17, Al-Burooj 1 to 11 and stopping signs
source: Written for quran/y5 lesson 32 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Stopping signs 1 rule card and examples)
intro: Lesson 32. Read the rule and say every example aloud. Point to each word in your mushaf. Then answer the questions.

panels.title: Two strong signs
points: م (ۘ): must stop here, or the meaning could change
لا (ۙ): do not stop here; carry on
Signs were added by scholars to help readers; they are not part of the revealed words

arabic.text: فَلَا يَحْزُنكَ قَوْلُهُمْ ۘ إِنَّا نَعْلَمُ مَا يُسِرُّونَ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ (٧٦)

keywords.def: stopping on a word, with a breath
a small mark above the line that tells us how to stop
a stop you must make (sign م)

questions.q: Read 36:76 with the stop at م.
Pupil PDF: for six sign examples, write 'must stop', 'do not stop' or 'carry on'. Today's rota group recites At-Tariq 1 to 12.
Extend: check whether your mushaf shows the same signs (some printings differ).
questions.a: Signs compared; differences noted for the teacher.

questions.q: Stretch: why is it important to say that the signs are not part of the revealed words?
questions.a: They were added later to help readers, like the dots and vowel marks.

questions.q: The sign لا (ۙ) above a word means ...
questions.a: A) do not stop here. لا: carry on reading.

questions.q: Think again: The mushaf has tiny letters above the line. Why might Allah's Book need signs that tell us where to stop?
questions.a: Stopping in the wrong place can change the meaning; the signs, added by scholars, help us stop where the meaning is safe.
